pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church CEP Academy - Wraparound Care
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Our wonderful staff, led by our wraparound care manager Mrs McCann, work hard to create a fun and safe environment for the children, with a wide range of activities available.
Breakfast Club
Our FREE breakfast club is open to all children from 7:55am until the start of the school day. A range of healthy breakfast food, and fun games and activities are on offer.
We also still offer early morning breakfast club from 7:30am, for £2.
All breakfast club attendance should be booked via Arbor to help us make sure that we have enough staff, and resources for the children.
After School Club
Flexible sessions run until 5:30pm, all children are given a healthy snack, and those who stay later are given a light tea. After school club has a huge variety of games, crafting activities, and outside activities, which the children thoroughly enjoy.
5:30pm £10.50 also includes a light tea at 5pm.
Dietary needs can be catered for - please speak to Mrs McCann.
Wraparound care should be booked via Arbor. Sessions must be booked and paid for in advance. If a payment has not been made, your child will regrettably be unable to attend. Where there is debt on an account your child will be unable to attend until this has been paid.

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church CEP Academy - After School Clubs
pageCache.text:
After School Clubs
How can my child attend a club?
In School terms 1, 3 and 5 an online form is sent out with a list of all the available clubs. Please select which club(s) you would like your child to attend. It is not guaranteed and Clubs are not first-come-first-served.
After School Activities are very popular and there is a limited number of spaces to each club. You will be notified via Dojo/Arbor if your child has been successful. If they haven't, they will be placed on the waiting list.
What happens if my child does not get into any club?
We do our best to ensure each child who applies for a club is offered a place at a club. If your child is unfortunate and does not receive any correspondence from Club Leaders they have applied for please do not be too disheartened. They will be placed on a waiting list and offered a club as soon as a place is available. Alternatively, if you require After-School Care, please book your child into our wraparound care 'Kids' Club' - further information can be obtained from the School Office.
When do the Clubs start?
On your child’s letter there will be a start and finish date. But usually the second full week into a new term and they finish the penultimate week of the seasonal term e.g. Christmas, Easter and Summer.
Where will my child go for their club?
Key Stage 1 children are collected by their Club Leader from their classroom. Key Stage 2 go straight to their Club Leaders allocated room.
When and where do I collect my child?
Clubs finish at 4pm. Please collect your child from the Key Stage 1 Gates.
Can anyone collect my child?
If your child is going to be collected by someone else please inform the School Office so they can make the Club Leader aware. Make sure it is a person known to your child and they are aware of the new arrangement. Children who attend Wraparound club will be escorted there. You will need to make your own arrangements with all other After School Clubs unrelated to the school.
Can my child walk home by him/herself?
Only Year 5 & 6 children may walk home with their parents’ permission, please use Arbor if you wish to consent to your child walking home after a club.

Personal, Social & Health Education
Jigsaw PSHE Curriculum
What is PSHE Education?
PSHE Education (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education) is a planned programme of learning through which children and young people acquire the knowledge, understanding and skills they need to successfully manage their lives – now and in the future. As part of a whole-school approach, PSHE Education develops the qualities and attributes pupils need to thrive as individuals, family members and members of society.
What do schools have to teach in PSHE Education?
According to the National Curriculum, every school needs to have a broad and balanced curriculum that:
From September 2020, primary schools in England also need to teach Relationships and Health Education as compulsory subjects and the Department for Education strongly recommends this should also include age-appropriate Sex Education.
Schools also have statutory responsibilities to safeguard their pupils (Keeping Children Safe in Education, DfE, 2021) and to uphold the Equality Act (2010).
How do we teach PSHE?
At Christ Church we follow the Jigsaw Programme, which supports all of these requirements and has children’s well-being at its heart. Every class (from Year R - 6) has a Jigsaw lesson each week.
Over the course of the year all pupils will study a unit on each of the 6 jigsaw pieces:
Each puzzle has six lesson plans accompanied by all of the teaching and learning materials needed to deliver them.
Through these units we aim for pupils to develop their skills and knowledge in an age-appropriate way in these areas to help pupils thrive and to prepare them for adolescence and adulthood:

Read Write Inc and Spelling Shed
At Christ Church we are a Read Write Inc School.
We use the Read Write Inc Phonics programme as soon as the children start in Reception and continue through year 1 and into year 2. When the children graduate from the phonics programme we move them onto the Spelling Shed programme for the rest of their time at Christ Church.
Read Write Inc phonics
The teaching of this programme is a method of learning centred around letter sounds and phonics, blending them together to read and write words and using these learnt sounds in their reading and writing. Using Read Write Inc phonics the children learn to read effortlessly so that they can put all their energy into comprehending what they read. It also allows them to spell effortlessly so that they can put their energy into composing what they write. The children are assessed and grouped according to their ability. They will work with a teacher or teaching assistant on the Read Write Inc phonics programme. At the end of each term the children will be assessed again by the Read Write Inc manager Mrs Carter and will then be put into new groups. In addition to the Read Write Inc programme the children will also be working on writing skills in their classes with their own class teacher to continue to develop their skills further.

Computing
Intent
We want children to see ICT as a fun and interesting subject which is relevant to their future. We aim to prepare our learners by giving them the opportunities to gain knowledge and develop skills that will equip them for an ever changing digital world. Knowledge and understanding of IT is of increasing importance for children’s future both at home and for employment. Our computing curriculum focuses on a progression of skills in digital literacy, computer science, information technology and online safety to ensure that children become competent in safely using, as well as understanding, technology.
When pupils leave Christ Church we intend for them to have a sound grasp of the basics of coding, spreadsheets, data bases and other creative tools. They should be able to confidently use technology safely and respectfully.
Implementation
We teach the National Curriculum, supported by a clear skills and knowledge progression via Purple Mash. Pupils have a weekly computing slot and the Purple Mash curriculum is formatted in a way which revisits topics regularly and builds on the children’s existing knowledge. To ensure a broad range of skills and understanding, Computing is taught across three main strands in every year group: digital literacy, computer science and information technology.
Information technology is about the use of computers for functional purposes, such as collecting and presenting information or using search technology.
Digital literacy is about the safe and responsible use of technology, including recognising its advantages for collaboration or communication.
Computer science provides children with an understanding of how computers and networks work. It also gives children the opportunity to learn basic computer programming.

Maths
Intent
At Christ Church Academy, our intent is to ensure that every child develops the mathematical knowledge, skills and confidence needed for future learning and life. We recognise maths as a vital subject that underpins critical thinking, problem solving and logical reasoning. Our aim is for all pupils to think mathematically, enabling them to question, explore, reason and make connections across different areas of the subject. Our inclusive approach ensures that every child, regardless of background or ability, is inspired to become a confident and resilient mathematician who can think deeply and make meaningful connections within and beyond the subject.
Implementation
As part of our mastery journey we have chosen to follow the White Rose Scheme to achieve a consistent coherent approach to teaching and learning (from Year R – 6). We teach the child, not just the curriculum, ensuring flexibility to adapt provision where necessary.
The curriculum is designed to build upon previous learning year-on-year (as a spiral curriculum) as well as revisiting prior learning to help retain knowledge. Maths is practised daily to ensure key mathematical concepts are embedded and children can recall this information to see the links between topics in maths.
In the Early Years Foundation Stage, children learn through a balance of adult-led teaching and rich, informal opportunities for mathematical thinking during child initiated activities. In KS1 and KS2, maths is taught for 1 hour and our lesson structure starts with Flash Back 4 or Daily Practice at the start of each lesson for 15 minutes to aid their long-term memory. Then pupils move onto the main session which introduces new concepts, modelling, guided practice and then independent tasks which focus on the arithmetic and then reasoning, problem solving and deepening understanding.
Lessons use a ‘Concrete, Pictorial and Abstract’ approach with carefully chosen manipulatives to guide children through their understanding of mathematical processes when a new concept is introduced (typically this in EYFS, KS1 and those who find a particular concept challenging).
Pupils are taught times tables in lessons, according to the National Curriculum. To aid with times tables retention, we use TT Rockstars and Numbots (for KS1).
download_for_offlineProgression of skills maths

Music
Intent
At Christ Church we aim for all pupils to enjoy music lessons and experiences and to see themselves as young musicians. We aim for pupils to be able to express themselves in different ways and through a variety of instruments (and voices). This may be in the form of listening and appraising pieces of music; through participating in musical activities (games, singing etc.); to performing and sharing their creations. Through our delivery of music lessons, we hope for all pupils to enhance their confidence in themselves. We see music as an opportunity for all to be able to succeed, regardless of other academic achievements. We provide pupils with the opportunity to experience a variety of music genres through different time periods and across different cultures. In doing so we hope to provide them with a wider knowledge base and musical experiences to be able to find styles they relish. Pupils are also shown the process behind developing and composing music to improvise with their own ideas - starting with writing their own music notes to performing it.
We hope that by the end of pupils’ time at Christ Church they have a passion for music and want to have the confidence to learn more about specific instruments from both a practical and theoretical side. Hopefully some pupils take this further and enhance their skills by taking up music as an extra-curricular activity and hobby.
Implementation
Music is taught every week in every year group from Year R through to Year 6. At Christ Church we follow Charanga and the Model Music Curriculum (Year R use the Original Scheme). Charanga provides teachers with week-by-week lesson support for each year group in the school. The Scheme supports all the requirements of the National Curriculum.
Structure of lessons:
Each term pupils cover a new Unit of Work. Each Unit of Work comprises of strands of musical learning which correspond with the National Curriculum for music:
Each Unit of Work will focus on different musical activities, which focus on different dimensions, skills and vocabulary. The strands of musical learning, presented within the lesson plans and the on-screen resources, are part of the learning spiral. Over time, children develop new musical skills and concepts, and re-visit established musical skills and concepts to consolidate previous learning.
Extra Curricular Activities:
Pupils are given the opportunity to attend music clubs after school every term this includes hand bells, choir and guitar club. Some of these clubs also offer trips as experiences and opportunities to perform e.g. Young Voices and church services.
Piano lessons are also offered by an external provider but held in school hours for our pupils.
Within the school year we provide other opportunities for external visitors to come in and share their knowledge and skills with our pupils either through workshops or performances. This is also celebrated as part of our Music Day which provides pupils with other musical opportunities such as a recording workshop.

Our Governors
Hello from the Governors
My name is Sue Dinsdale and I am the Chair of Governors. I have a long history with Christ Church Primary and my own children, now fully grown and with children of their own all attended here.
As a governing body we bring a wealth of knowledge and experience to the role including backgrounds in school leadership, teaching, accountancy, health and safety, the church and safeguarding.
As critical friends we regularly hold the senior leadership to account through meetings and school visits and we take an active interest in everyday school life.
Our prime focus is on ensuring that the strategic vision for the school is delivered in a way that is not only financially sustainable but ensures that every pupil, family and every one of our amazing members of staff is valued, cared for and can be the best versions of themselves.
I look forward to continuing my involvement with the school's journey and on behalf of all of the governors I wish you all peace and good fortune.Sue Dinsdale

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church CEP Academy - PE & Sport
pageCache.text:
PE & Sport
PE Vision
Intent
At Christ Church we aim for pupils to look forward to and enjoy high quality PE lessons in a safe and supportive environment. We believe this is important to not only equip pupils with skills that will benefit them in their transition to secondary school and beyond but to also help them to lead healthy lifestyles. Pupils will be educated around the importance of this so they can strive to live healthy, active lives regardless of their sporting abilities.
We intend to deliver high-quality teaching and learning opportunities that inspire all children to reach their potential in physical education, school sport and physical activity. We want our pupils to engage in lessons that are enjoyable, challenging and accessible to all.
Children should be inspired by PE lessons to participate in after school clubs or to take up sports activities outside of the school environment.
Implementation
The PE long term curriculum map is planned and structured to allow the children to build upon prior knowledge and continue to improve their skills over time by returning to the sports each year within each key stage. We use the PE hub lesson plans which set out lessons and learning objectives so that all PE lessons are sequenced and progressive and provide children with opportunities to improve their skills.
All pupils partake in two different sporting activities, twice a week, each term. Children from Years R-4 swim three terms a year in the school pool, which we think is not only a crucial life skill, but also vital for pupils to do based upon the geographic location of our school – by the sea. Dance and gymnastics are taught for one term each year from Year R-6. We have also chosen 7 sports (athletics, tennis, football, basketball, hockey, cricket and OAA) which are taught for one term a year from Years 3-6. Years R-2 participate in skills-based units to equip them with the skills they need to begin learning the sports in Year 3. These sports were decided upon as they were voted for by pupils based upon their interests - yet still making sure we cover the breadth of activities stated on the National Curriculum.
Up until 2025-26 our PE lessons were delivered by teaching staff or specialist coaches. We provide CPD opportunities for staff that are led by specialists to help promote the quality of our teaching.
We enhance our curriculum further by providing additional opportunities outside of PE lessons for pupils to participate in. There are regular opportunities, for all year groups, to take part in events and competitions organised by Shepway Sports Trust and other outside agencies. We also offer a wide range of after school clubs each term.

Attendance
Learning
At Christ Church we pack as much learning as we can into each day. Not a minute is wasted. Each day your child learns maths skills and literacy skills and is immersed in a rich and varied curriculum through the Christ Church Experience. If children miss a day they will find that the learning has moved on and it can be a real struggle to catch up. This can damage your child’s self-esteem as well as their progress.
Confidence
It can be tempting to keep a child off if they are finding school hard. Maybe they are struggling with their learning, with friendships or just don’t want to separate from their special adults. Keeping children off for these reasons will make it even harder tor them to eventually come back to school. Come and talk to someone at school– we want to help
Behaviour
Children love routine and school is built on routine. Children understand what is expected of them at school and see the benefits of attending school and trying their hardest. They feel safe and secure within these boundaries. We know that children with poor attendance find it hardest to behave in school as they do not understand the rules and routines as well as the others, they also miss opportunities to be rewarded for their hard work. It is often these children who also have the most challenging behaviour at home as their routine is unpredictable.
Friendships
We all know how fast new crazes come and go. What is ‘in’ one day will be ‘out’ the next. Children’s games and friendships move at this fast pace too. Children who miss days at school are likely to come back to find that their friends have moved on to new games and they are likely to struggle to find their place again.
What is good enough attendance?
We know that children get ill and whilst many children manage to achieve 100% attendance over the year this is not the expectation for all children. The Local Authority suggest that children should be at school at least 97% of the time.
Many people think that 90% attendance is good enough but did you know that this adds up to 20 days absent a year? A full month of school! During the time your child is at primary school this adds up to half a year of absence!
There are various reward systems in place to celebrate good attendance. We have a weekly '£5 for 5' prize draw! All children who have achieved 100% are entered and the winner is awarded with £5 in Celebration Assembly. A weekly league also runs throughout the year- the class who are 'Top of League' are rewarded with a treat.
At Christ Church we recognise that good attendance is a whole family achievement so we reward families by having a 'Family Prize Draw' at the end of each term. The winning family are presented with an experience which allows them to celebrate together. For example: a restaurant voucher, theatre voucher, sports centre experience, Zoo visit to name a few.
Our Arbor app allows families to view current attendance figures in real time, ensuring transparency. Letters are sent out every term to parents whose children achieve less than 95% and 'Attendance Success' meetings are arranged with a DSL to co-construct a plan to overcome barriers. Referrals and meetings take place with an attendance officer from KCC where attendance falls below 90%. At this point families are at risk of fines or prosecutions.
Punctual and ready to learn
The school gates open at 8:25 and close at 8:40. Children are required to be in class by 8:45. After this time children will need to come into the front office to be registered using the InVentry system. Children arriving after 8:50 will be marked as ‘late’. Children who arrive after 9:00 will be marked with an unauthorised absence unless there is a genuine reason for them attending late e.g. medical appointment, woke up with high temperature and now feeling better etc.
Children hate to be late for school. They often feel embarrassed walking into class when lessons have started. They may have missed teacher input which will make it hard for them to understand the lesson.
Contacting the school
If your child is too ill to attend then you are required to phone the school or leave a message on the absence line that morning giving the reason for absence. If we do not hear from you a link to a MS Form will be sent out to you to submit. If we do not receive a response from the link then the absence will be recorded as unauthorised and too many of these can lead to a fine!
Children, like adults often feel under the weather first thing in the morning. Usually once they are dressed, have had a good breakfast and are in school they perk up. Sometimes you may even decide to give them a dose of Calpol before school. If you fill in a medical form at the front office we will even be able to give them a second dose at lunchtime. If we are worried that your child is too ill for school we will phone you straight away and ask for them to be collected. So if you are not sure give them a try!
Give your child some paracetamol in the morning, take their temperature again after a couple of hours and bring them to school late if they are feeling better.
Stay at home with
Chicken pox: until spots have scabbed over
Come to school with
If you are having difficulties getting your child to school please come and talk to us and we will do what we can to help.
Headache
Minor illness or injury

Attendance
Learning
At Christ Church we pack as much learning as we can into each day. Not a minute is wasted. Each day your child learns maths skills and literacy skills and is immersed in a rich and varied curriculum through the Christ Church Experience. If children miss a day they will find that the learning has moved on and it can be a real struggle to catch up. This can damage your child’s self-esteem as well as their progress.
Confidence
It can be tempting to keep a child off if they are finding school hard. Maybe they are struggling with their learning, with friendships or just don’t want to separate from their special adults. Keeping children off for these reasons will make it even harder tor them to eventually come back to school. Come and talk to someone at school– we want to help
Behaviour

They feel safe and secure within these boundaries. We know that children with poor attendance find it hardest to behave in school as they do not understand the rules and routines as well as the others, they also miss opportunities to be rewarded for their hard work. It is often these children who also have the most challenging behaviour at home as their routine is unpredictable.

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church CEP Academy - Family Liaison Officer
pageCache.text:
Family Liaison Officer (FLO)
I am thrilled to introduce myself to you as the Family Liaison Officer (FLO) at Christ Church. My name is Jo Diwell, and I have had the pleasure of serving our school community for over 20 years. I am dedicated to supporting the children and families here at Christ Church. If you ever need any assistance or information regarding your child, please do not hesitate to get in touch. I am here to help in any way I can. What is a FLO?
The FLO plays an important role in supporting parents, carers, and pupils with any barriers or problems that may be affecting their home or school life, and in turn, impacting the children's learning. A FLO is available to listen, provide support, and help families find the right assistance they need. Additionally, they organise courses for both adults and children, as well as various get-togethers such as coffee mornings. You will find information on these via the dojo or our weekly newsletter. If you ever feel the need to reach out, whether for a chat or for some guidance, please do not hesitate to contact me, I am here to support and assist you in any way I can.
I am available to contact in the following ways - maybe it's a cup of tea and a chat in person, maybe through the Dojo app, or a quick phone call or email, whatever works best for you and your family . I'm usually on the playground in the morning or afternoon, so feel free to drop by whenever it's convenient for you. It's always lovely to have a chat and connect with you. Looking forward to catching up soon!
j.diwell@christ-church-folkestone.kent.sch.uk
The hours I work are:
Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8.30 – 3.30pm
These are just a few things I support our community with:
Parenting advice
Family relationships
Challenging behaviour
Self-esteem issues
Bereavement
Domestic Violence
Healthy eating
Health issues
Well-being groups for children
Courses for parents

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church CEP Academy - Pupil & Family Support
pageCache.text:
Pupil & Family Support
Tiers of Support
Learning about our own emotional wellbeing is an integral part of the curriculum at Christ Church CEP Academy.
Children are taught about how their wellbeing can be positively and negatively impacted by their lifestyle and by events around them. They are taught how to recognise changes in their own wellbeing and taught strategies to manage their emotions.
The aim is to enable our children to flourish into confident and emotionally resilient individuals.
Tier 1
Tier 1 represents the quality learning experiences which are available to every child. These experiences are largely organised and delivered through the Jigsaw curriculum.
Peer mediators
Tier 2
Targeted, short term additional support for pupils who are struggling which might include:
Meditation/Yoga club
Social skills group
Environmental therapy
Tier 3
For pupils with longer term or more complex emotional needs there are a range of support options in school e.g.
or referral to external agencies e.g.
Rising Sun
Counselling
Young Carers
School Nurse Service
Family Support
At Christ Church we understand that families have their ups and downs and we understand that this can have an impact on our pupils and their learning.
All of our staff are passionate about helping families as much as we can.
We might be able to:
You can approach any of our staff if you have a concern. Mrs Diwell (Family Liaison Officer) and Miss Perkins (Deputy Headteacher) would also be able to provide further support.
If you are experiencing a problem which we are unable to help with as a school we will signpost you to an organisation that can
These agencies include:
We acknowledge the trauma which a bereavement can bring to a family. If you and your child have been affected please contact us and we can work together to support you and your child.
Offer advice about behaviour at home
Make changes in school to support children
School Nurses
Early Help
Social Services
Citizens Advice Bureau
Counselling Services
Local Churches and Charities
Adult Education
Domestic Abuse Services
Migrant Help

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ Church CEP Academy - School Meals
pageCache.text:
School Meals
The school has its own canteen providing hot and cold lunches daily. Meals are prepared by Independent Catering staff and are designed to provide a sustaining, nutritionally balanced meal.
https://www.independentcatering.co.uk/primary-schools/#info Families on Income Support or Job Seekers Allowance are entitled to a free meal and should complete a form online, the web address is available from the School Office to claim this entitlement or download and print of the form from the KCC Logo down the page. For children who are not entitled to a free school meal, the cost is £3.00 a day, payable at the beginning of each week via Arbor. Children can choose to bring their own packed lunch from home, which should contain healthy option choices with no chocolate or fizzy drinks. The only other food allowed in school is a piece of fruit, which can be eaten during the morning break. Children are encouraged to drink water throughout the day. Water bottles may be purchased from the school office.
Free school meals
If you have children under 19 and in full-time education, you may be able to get free school meals for them. Am I eligible?
To be eligible for free school meals the pupil must be attending a state-maintained school or receiving alternative education approved by Kent County Council and the pupil's family must be in receipt of one of the following benefits. Please provide the relevant proof of identity, as detailed below.: Income Support
Income Based Jobseekers Allowance
Child Tax Credit (not including Working Tax Credit)
If the household income is below £16190.
Guaranteed Element of State Pension Credit
Proof of support under part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999.
An Income-related Employment and Support Allowance If you think you may be entitled to free school meals, please request a form from the school office or alternatively, please download and print-off the Free School Meals form (PDF, 93k) from the KCC Logo above.
Universal Free School Meals
Children in years R to 2 are eligible for free school meals under the Government's Universal Free School Meal initiative. If you are in receipt of the correct benefits you must still put in an application for your child to receive free school meals as per the above information. This can be done on the internet by visiting : www.kent.gov.uk Education and children Free school meals The application should take about 10 minutes to complete.
The help line number is: 03000416464
